headline: Master Edge AI Performance on Android: Stop Guessing, Start Profiling
summary: Optimize your AI models for Android devices by mastering the Android Studio Power Profiler to balance performance, energy consumption, and heat.
details: Deploying AI models on Android devices can lead to performance issues like lag and overheating if not properly optimized. The Android Studio Power Profiler is essential for developers to move beyond basic battery percentage and understand the complex interplay between CPU, GPU, and NPU utilization.

The core challenge in Edge AI is the 'Trilemma'—balancing model accuracy, inference speed, and energy consumption. Developers must find the Pareto Optimal point where the model is good enough across all three metrics to satisfy users.

Google's AICore service revolutionizes on-device AI by managing models as shared resources, similar to Google Play Services. This approach drastically reduces APK size, redundant memory allocation, and improves overall efficiency by avoiding multiple copies of the same model.

Effective profiling requires understanding which hardware component is running your model. High CPU usage might indicate the model is falling back from the NPU due to unsupported operators. Conversely, high memory power consumption suggests the need for quantization.

Quantizing models from 32-bit floats (FP32) to 8-bit integers (INT8) not only reduces memory footprint by 4x but also significantly enhances energy efficiency by minimizing transistor activity. Pruning further optimizes models by removing unnecessary neurons, leading to faster computations and quicker return to low-power states.

To accurately profile Edge AI performance, developers need a controlled workload. Implementing a real-time image classification pipeline using TensorFlow Lite, with togglable CPU and GPU delegates, allows for direct observation of energy shifts in the Power Profiler.
caption:

headline_marked: [[Command & Conquer Generals]] ported to macOS, iPhone, iPad
headline: Command & Conquer Generals ported to macOS, iPhone, iPad
summary: The original 2003 engine has been compiled for ARM64, offering native performance on Apple devices with custom touch controls.
details: Command & Conquer Generals: Zero Hour can now run natively on macOS, iPhone, and iPad thanks to a new port. This project utilizes the original 2003 engine, compiled for ARM64 architecture, ensuring real performance without emulation.

The port features touch controls specifically designed for Real-Time Strategy (RTS) gameplay, including tap-to-select, drag-to-box, long-press for deselection, two-finger scrolling, and pinch-to-zoom.

This achievement was made possible by fbraz3/GeneralsX, which handled the heavy lifting of the macOS and Linux port. This fork further extends compatibility to iOS and iPadOS, alongside a suite of engine fixes.
The project leverages EA's GPL v3 source release. While the engine code is open-source, users must provide their own game assets, which can be obtained from platforms like Steam for around $5.
Building the port requires Xcode, brew, and an Apple Developer team. The process involves compiling DirectX 8 through a chain of translators (DXVK, Vulkan, MoltenVK) to Apple's Metal graphics API.

This port was developed as a human-AI collaboration, with engineering directed by Anthropic's Claude Code and playtested by Ammaar Reshi on real devices. The detailed engineering log is available in the project's documentation.
